title: From Agent Authorization to AI Production Evaluation: QCon AI New York 2026
gist: A QCon AI New York 2026 (Dec 15-16) program preview arguing that production AI engineering has become systems engineering: agent identity/authorization (1Password), guardrails for a Kubernetes ops agent (LinkedIn), a consolidated multi-tenant inference platform (Netflix, ~1M req/s across 300+ models), and post-deployment evaluation with cheap-classifier gating of LLMs (DoorDash). Inference economics (latency, tokens, routing, cost) are framed as first-class architectural constraints.

insights.claim: Production AI engineering is shifting from model behavior to system behavior: bounded agent execution authority, context/state management, and deterministic control planes wrapped around probabilistic models.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Value in the AI stack is migrating toward control-plane, orchestration and governance tooling around models, not just the models themselves.
insights.quote: AI engineering has become systems engineering.
insights.locator: Across this year’s program, one shift is unmistakable

insights.claim: Harness engineering, continuous evaluation, observability, and policy enforcement are becoming core infrastructure for AI systems rather than optional add-ons.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Signals durable demand for AI eval, observability and policy/guardrail vendors as a budget line in production AI.
insights.quote: Harness engineering, continuous evaluation, observability, and policy enforcement are becoming core infrastructure.

insights.claim: Inference economics — latency, token usage, model routing, and cost — are now first-class architectural constraints in AI system design, not implementation details.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Cost-per-inference pressure favors model routing, smaller/cheaper models and inference-optimization tooling; watch for margin pressure on pure frontier-model API spend.
insights.quote: inference economics such as latency, token usage, model routing, and cost are now first-class architectural constraints, not implementation details.

insights.claim: The emerging AI engineering discipline is absorbing practices from distributed systems, security, platform engineering, and SRE, aimed at making AI systems reliable, observable, controllable, and economical.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Incumbent DevOps/security/platform vendors have a natural path to expand into AI operations spend.
insights.locator: Hien added that the emerging discipline

insights.claim: Traditional identity systems assume one human principal, a stable role, a bounded session and an accountable person, whereas AI agents may act for multiple users, invoke unenumerated tools, spawn subagents and run unsupervised — breaking these assumptions.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Agentic AI creates a new IAM/secrets-management problem space; identity vendors positioning for non-human/agent identity are worth tracking.
insights.locator: Traditional identity systems generally assume one human principal

insights.claim: Key open problems for agent authorization are delegated authority across chains of agents, auditability across multi-hop tool calls, and granting task-sufficient access without placing credentials or secrets into the agent's context.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Secrets brokering and agent audit trails are emerging product categories adjacent to password/secrets managers.
insights.locator: The keynote will cover delegated authority

insights.claim: Both broadly privileged long-lived service accounts and overly narrow permissions fail for agents — the former is unsafe and the latter prevents the agent from completing its work.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Existing service-account patterns are inadequate, pointing to demand for dynamic, scoped, just-in-time credentialing.
insights.locator: Nancy will also examine the limitations

insights.claim: LinkedIn runs a Kubernetes-based compute platform of more than 500,000 nodes and five million pods, and has built an operations agent usable via Slack, coding-agent plugins and automated workflows to investigate deployment failures.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Large-scale operators are already deploying AI agents in infra operations, validating the AIOps/agentic SRE market.

insights.claim: When an ops agent moves from explaining problems to acting on production infrastructure, LinkedIn requires server-side rate limits, protection on delete and scale-down operations, access controls, bounded actions, and peer approval for production changes.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop approval and action bounding are the practical gate on agent autonomy in infra — limits near-term full-automation claims.
insights.locator: The session focuses on the engineering controls

insights.claim: LinkedIn turns recurring operational work into reusable agent skills, mining JIRA history and prior support conversations to identify problems those skills can handle.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Historical ticket/support data is a strategic asset for agent training — benefits ticketing platforms holding that data.
insights.locator: Nathani will also describe how the team

insights.claim: After a five-year consolidation effort, Netflix's shared model-serving platform handles approximately one million inference requests per second across more than 300 models, spanning recommendations, commerce and LLM applications.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Mature operators consolidate classic ML and GenAI onto one serving layer — a template favoring unified inference platforms over per-model stacks.
insights.locator: The resulting platform handles approximately one million

insights.claim: Netflix's single multi-tenant inference platform must support latency regimes from tens of milliseconds to over 300 milliseconds, requiring a common deployment contract and a clear boundary between business logic and model logic.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous latency needs are a key design constraint for inference infrastructure vendors.
insights.locator: Rajat will examine the architectural and organizational trade-offs

insights.claim: Consolidating model serving lets ML teams stop rebuilding deployment infrastructure per model and focus on modeling, though it introduces its own operational costs and ongoing challenges.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Platform consolidation is a productivity lever but not free — factor ongoing platform ops costs into AI infra ROI.
insights.locator: The session will also cover what consolidation changed

themes.theme: Post-deployment AI evaluation and cost cascades

insights.claim: DoorDash's Alchemy moderation platform uses a lower-cost in-house classifier to gate access to a more expensive LLM, so roughly 90% of content classified as clearly acceptable never reaches the expensive layers.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Cascade architectures sharply cut LLM inference spend — a headwind for per-token API revenue growth and tailwind for small-model/classifier tooling.
insights.quote: Approximately 90% of content classified as clearly acceptable never reaches the more expensive layers.
insights.locator: Alchemy is a content-agnostic moderation platform

insights.claim: Evaluating deployed AI decisions is hard because there is often no clean ground truth and judgments are nondeterministic; DoorDash's harness uses shadow-mode testing, backtesting on historical production data, labeling, and metrics tied to incident reduction rather than model accuracy alone.
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Business-outcome-based eval (incident reduction) is replacing accuracy metrics — relevant to evaluation tooling vendors' positioning.
insights.locator: Bruna will discuss an evaluation harness

insights.claim: LLM judgments can be recycled as training data for a cheaper classifier, progressively reducing latency and inference costs over time (a distillation-style flywheel).
insights.speaker: Artenisa Chatziou
insights.so_what: Expect enterprise LLM spend per task to decline over time as workloads get distilled into cheaper in-house models.
